entries.title: Indoor infrared sauna comparison
entries.description: Compare the documented dimensions, capacity and electrical requirements of the current indoor infrared sauna set.
entries.heading: Compare indoor infrared saunas by size, capacity and electrical requirements
introduction: The research catalog currently contains 24 infrared products documented for indoor placement in the United States. The table on this page shows the eight published configurations whose current source review supports a public comparison. Model pages keep dimensions, capacity, materials and core electrical values attached to the configuration they describe; an open field remains visible until its own source review is complete.
This is a specification comparison, not a hands-on test or a quality ranking. A configuration appears only when its product type, heat type and placement are documented in the source record.

sections.heading: Cabinet dimensions do not define the full room envelope
paragraphs: Where exterior measurements are documented, they make it possible to compare the cabinet bodies. The current records do not contain reviewed installation clearances, so those figures cannot establish that a cabin fits tightly between walls or below a ceiling.

When room dimensions are entered in the sauna finder, a cabinet that fits remains under needs verification until the missing clearance information has been checked in the instructions for that exact model.

sections.heading: Electrical requirements vary among 120-volt models
paragraphs: Within the first source-complete subset, Peak documents 10 amps for the Mini, 15 amps for the Crown and Shasta, and a dedicated 20-amp circuit for the Everest and Fuji. JNH lists 120 volts and 15 amps for the Tosi 1-Person and Tosi 2-Person and says a standard 110-volt, 15-amp outlet is sufficient for its one- and two-person Tosi models. The Tosi Red 4-Person requires dedicated 120-volt, 20-amp service.

A voltage filter is therefore useful for narrowing the catalog, but it does not approve an outlet or circuit for installation. The plug, circuit requirement and model instructions still need to be checked together.

entries.title: JNH Lifestyles sauna configurations
entries.description: A source-based view of the JNH Lifestyles Tosi and Arki sauna configurations in the current US comparison set.
entries.heading: The documented JNH range spans compact indoor cabins and one outdoor model
introduction: Four JNH Lifestyles configurations are currently recorded. The indoor Tosi group covers one, two and four seats, while the Arki Outdoor Duo is documented for outdoor placement and two people.

The records describe model-specific dimensions and power information. They do not combine the four configurations into one generic product or assume that specifications carry from one size to another.

sections.heading: Capacity and placement separate the four configurations
paragraphs: The Tosi 1-Person is the narrowest cabin in the recorded group at 35.5 inches wide. The Tosi 2-Person increases the documented exterior width to 47.3 inches, and the Tosi Red 4-Person reaches 70.9 inches. The Arki Outdoor Duo is a separate outdoor configuration rather than an outdoor version inferred from the Tosi line.

sections.heading: The larger configurations have different circuit requirements
paragraphs: All four records list 120 volts. JNH specifies 15 amps for the Tosi 1-Person and Tosi 2-Person and states that a standard 110-volt, 15-amp outlet is sufficient for its one- and two-person Tosi models. The Tosi Red 4-Person and Arki Outdoor Duo document dedicated 20-amp service.
The product page for each configuration shows the unresolved fields alongside the documented values.

entries.title: Infrared sauna electrical requirements
entries.description: Learn which model-specific electrical facts need to be checked beyond the voltage printed on an infrared sauna listing.
entries.heading: A 120-volt sauna can still require a different circuit and receptacle
introduction: Voltage is only one part of an infrared sauna's electrical specification. The model record may also identify rated current, required circuit capacity, a dedicated circuit, connection method and plug type.
Those fields need to refer to the same configuration. A value from a smaller cabin or another size in the product family is not a substitute for the instructions supplied with the selected model.

sections.heading: Read each supply option as a complete set
paragraphs: Each configuration linked from this guide has one recorded electrical supply option. Where the manufacturer record states a required circuit or dedicated circuit, the site keeps that requirement with the voltage rather than reducing the product to a voltage badge.
If a future configuration documents alternative supply options, each option will be evaluated separately. Requirements that belong to the same option must all be satisfied together.

sections.heading: An open circuit field is not permission to use any outlet
paragraphs: The Mini and Crown records document 120-volt power information but leave the required circuit rating unresolved. JNH states that a standard 110-volt, 15-amp outlet is sufficient for its one- and two-person Tosi models, while their configuration-specific specifications list 120 volts and 15 amps. The finder keeps these documented requirements attached to the exact model.

Final installation should follow the documentation for the exact configuration and the applicable local requirements. The finder does not size wiring, approve adapters or replace review by a qualified professional.
